Prof. '''Zvi HaCohen''' (last name HaCohen or Cohen, [[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]:  צבי הכהן, born 1947) is an Israeli scientist who, since August 2010, has served as Rector of [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]] (BGU) until 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://in.bgu.ac.il/en/Pages/management/rector.aspx|title=Ben-Gurion University of the Negev – Rector|website=in.bgu.ac.il|access-date=28 December 2017}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==

HaCohen was born in Cluj, [[Romania]] in 1947, immigrated to Israel in 1950 and was raised in [[Rehovot]]. He received a [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] Degree in chemistry in 1970, an [[Master of Science|MSc]] Degree in [[organic chemistry]] in 1974, both from [[Bar-Ilan University]] and a PhD in organic chemistry in 1978, from the [[Weizmann Institute of Science]]. Between 1978 and 1981, he was a post doctoral fellow in the Department of Radiology at [[Harvard Medical School]].

== Professional career ==
HaCohen published over 120 scientific papers, registered 8 patents and edited 3 books. During his PhD studies he developed a method for dry [[Ozone|ozonation]], which enabled regioselective [[hydroxylation]] of [[Carbon–carbon bond|tertiary carbon]] atoms of [[hydrocarbon]]s, with a yield of 100%, in comparison to a few tenths of a percent, previously.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cohen|first1=Z|last2=Keinan|first2=E|last3=Mazur|first3=Y|last4=Varkony|first4=T.H.|year=1975|title=Method for stereoselective hydroxylation of saturated compounds on silica gel|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=40 |issue=14|pages=2141–2142|doi=10.1021/jo00902a035}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cohen|first1=Zvi.|last2=Keinan|first2=Ehud.|last3=Mazur|first3=Yehuda.|last4=Ulman|first4=Aharon.|date=1 July 1976|title=Hydroxylation with ozone on silica gel. The synthesis of 1.alpha.,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3|journal=The Journal of Organic Chemistry|volume=41|issue=15|pages=2651–2652|doi=10.1021/jo00877a035|pmid=181551|issn=0022-3263}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Organic Syntheses|last1=Cohen|first1=Zvi|last2=Varkony|first2=Haim|last3=Keinan|first3=Ehud|last4=Mazur|first4=Yehuda|date=1 January 2003|publisher=John Wiley & Sons, Inc.|isbn=9780471264224|language=en|doi=10.1002/0471264180.os059.25}}</ref> As a postdoctoral fellow, he designed a new contrast agent for computed tomography of liver metastasis, made of [[Iodine|iodinated]] [[starch]] particles, which enabled the detection of [[liver]] [[metastasis]], smaller than 2&nbsp;mm.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cohen|first1=Z.|last2=Seltzer|first2=S. E.|last3=Davis|first3=M. A.|last4=Hanson|first4=R. N.|date=1 December 1981|title=Iodinated starch particles: new contrast material for computed tomography of the liver|journal=Journal of Computer Assisted Tomography|volume=5|issue=6|pages=843–846|issn=0363-8715|pmid=7320289|doi=10.1097/00004728-198112000-00010|s2cid=30923918}}</ref> During his career at BGU, he studied the [[biochemistry]] and developed the [[biotechnology]] of the production of several [[Omega-6 fatty acid|omega 6]] and [[Omega-3 fatty acid|omega 3]] [[Polyunsaturated fat|polyunsaturated]] fatty acids (e.g., [[arachidonic acid]], [[eicosapentaenoic acid]], [[Dihomo-γ-linolenic acid|dihomogammalinolenic acid]]) from [[Microphyte|micro algae]]<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Cohen|first1=Zvi|last2=Norman|first2=Helen A.|last3=Heimer|first3=Yair M.|date=1 January 1995|publisher=Karger Publishers|volume=77|pages=1–31|language=english|doi=10.1159/000424462|title=Plants in Human Nutrition|series=World Review of Nutrition and Dietetics|isbn=978-3-8055-6101-3}}</ref><ref name="Khozin">{{Cite journal|last1=Khozin-Goldberg|first1=Inna|last2=Bigogno|first2=Chiara|last3=Shrestha|first3=Pushkar|last4=Cohen|first4=Zvi|date=1 October 2002|title=Nitrogen Starvation Induces the Accumulation of Arachidonic Acid in the Freshwater Green Alga ''Parietochloris Incisa'' (trebuxiophyceae)1|journal=Journal of Phycology|volume=38|issue=5|pages=991–994|doi=10.1046/j.1529-8817.2002.01160.x|s2cid=84752670|issn=1529-8817}}</ref> and was involved with the development of the biotechnology of the micro alga [[Haematococcus pluvialis]],<ref name="Khozin"/> culminated in the establishment of a commercial facility in [[Ketura, Israel]].

== Academic and related positions ==

Between 1980 and 1981, . Hacohen had an appointment of assistant professor at the [[University of Massachusetts Medical School]] at [[Worcester, Massachusetts]]. In 1981, he moved to the Desert Research Institute of Ben-Gurion University at Sde Boker. Between 1996 and 2010, he served as chairman of the faculty association of the university and from 2005 to 2010, also as the chairman of Coordination Council of the Faculty Associations of the Israeli Universities. In 2010, he was elected as Rector of Ben-Gurion University of the Negev. In 2015 he was elected to chair the Rectors' Forum of Israeli Universities.

== Honors ==

1986–97 – Incumbent of the Sonnefeldt Career Development Chair in Desert Research.

1998 – Recipient of the Pasternak prize for Agricultural Research.

2005 – incumbent of the Maks and Rochelle Etingin Professorial chair in Desert Research.

2016 – Honorary professorship recipient, Babes-Bolyai university, Cluj, Romania.
